title: Michigan's September workforce data: what the numbers say, and what they don't

voices.name: Brian
voices.description: Deep and resonant, comforting and steady.

voices.name: Sarah
voices.description: Warm and reassuring, with a calm, confident delivery.

chapters.headline: The headline figure is the least interesting part
points: The September workforce edition is published: labor data through August, program planning, AI task analysis
Evidence cutoff: September 26, 2026; every figure comes from the public September edition
August unemployment was 5.0% — and that rate is not the story
chapters.takeaway: Start with what the numbers actually say, not with the headline rate.

chapters.headline: A calm rate can conceal a shrinking labor force
points: Employment and the labor force both fell by 25,000 in the month
chapters.takeaway: When the labor force itself shrinks by 25,000, the unemployment rate stays deceptively calm.

chapters.headline: More slack than the headline shows
points: The broader U-6 measure: 9.1% — for the July 2025–June 2026 window, not an August reading
Recent graduates faced about 5.6% unemployment in Q2; degree-based underemployment 42%
Consumer sentiment fell to 48.1 in September, from 51.7 in August
chapters.takeaway: These measures count different populations — the report never adds them together, and treats warning signals as signals, not forecasts.

chapters.headline: The first three
points: Redesign narrow task training first — typing, data-entry, routine transaction curricula need immediate review
Retain foundations in AI-exposed professions: AI exposure alone does not establish occupation decline
Prioritize Michigan demand and replacement needs over national projections alone
chapters.takeaway: Match program capacity to verified regional demand — and keep the foundations while tasks change.

chapters.headline: Bridges, cohorts, and the radiology test
points: Build skills bridges before layoffs: a real receiving role, supervised learning, work samples
Plan by graduation cohort: 2027 credentials, 2028 associate, 2030 bachelor's, 2032 and beyond for longer pathways
Radiology: projections show growth, not obsolescence — adapt the curriculum, keep the foundations
chapters.takeaway: The cohort years are decision horizons, not occupation expiry dates.

chapters.headline: Every number traceable, every limit stated
points: September 27: the project's first connector-triggered audited release
All 6 downloadable assets and 33 ZIP member hashes verified after publication
The edition declares no program obsolete on a speculative date
chapters.takeaway: In a space full of confident forecasts, restraint is a feature.
